questions.question: Who is the author of the story 'The Village Judge'?
questions.explanation: The story 'The Village Judge' is written by Prem Chand.

questions.question: Who were the two 'great friends' mentioned at the beginning of the story?
questions.explanation: The text states, 'Jumman Sheikh and Algu Chaudhuri were great friends'.

questions.question: What did Jumman's old aunt possess that Jumman wanted?
questions.explanation: Jumman's aunt had a small piece of property which she was persuaded to transfer to his name.

questions.question: How was the aunt treated before the property was transferred to Jumman?

options.D: She was made to work in the fields

questions.explanation: So long as the property was not transferred, the aunt was treated with great kindness and respect.

questions.question: Who was Jumman's wife?
questions.explanation: Jumman's wife is named Kariman in the story.

questions.question: What happened to the treatment of the aunt after the property was transferred?

options.C: She was given a monthly allowance
options.D: She was asked to leave the village

questions.explanation: When the property was transferred, all kindness vanished and Jumman and his wife became harsh and rude.

questions.question: What did the aunt request from Jumman when she could no longer bear the harsh treatment?

options.B: Some money to cook and eat separately

questions.explanation: She told Jumman, 'You should give me some money. I shall cook and eat separately'.

questions.question: What was Jumman's rude reply to his aunt's request for money?

options.B: Money does not grow on trees here.

questions.explanation: Jumman replied rudely, 'Money does not grow on trees here'.

questions.question: What did the aunt threaten to do after Jumman's rude reply?
questions.explanation: The aunt grew angry and threatened to call a panchayat.

questions.question: How did Jumman react to the threat of a panchayat?

options.B: He welcomed it, saying he hated daily quarrels.
options.D: He tried to stop her from going.

questions.explanation: Jumman said, 'Certainly, have a panchayat by all means... I hate these daily quarrels myself'.

questions.question: What did the aunt use for support while running from village to village?
questions.explanation: She ran from village to village with a stick in her hand to support her.

questions.question: Did most people in the village offer comfort to the old woman?

options.B: No, most did not hear her story with care or offer comfort.
options.D: They told her to go to the police.

questions.explanation: Most people did not hear the story with care and attention and did not offer her any comfort.

questions.question: Why did Algu initially say he would not 'open his mouth' at the panchayat?

options.A: He was afraid of the aunt.
options.C: He was not a member of the panchayat.

questions.explanation: Algu said, 'Jumman is an old friend of mine. I cannot quarrel with him'.

questions.question: What question did the aunt ask Algu that 'echoed in his heart'?

options.B: Will you hesitate to say the honest thing because you fear a quarrel?
options.D: Can you be the Chief Judge?

questions.explanation: The aunt asked, 'Son, will you hesitate to say the honest thing, because you fear a quarrel?' and these words echoed in his heart.

questions.question: Where did the panchayat meet?
questions.explanation: The panchayat met under a tree one evening.

questions.question: Who did the old woman name as the Chief Judge?
questions.explanation: She said, 'Do you accept Algu Chaudhuri? I name him as Chief Judge'.

questions.question: How did Jumman feel when Algu was named Chief Judge?

options.B: He was overjoyed but hid it.

questions.explanation: Jumman was overjoyed, but he hid his feelings and replied: 'Let it be Algu Chaudhuri'.

questions.question: According to the aunt, who lives in the heart of the panch?
questions.explanation: The aunt said, 'God lives in the heart of the panch'.

questions.question: The aunt said that nobody can sell his ________ for friendship.
questions.explanation: The aunt replied gravely: 'Son, nobody can sell his conscience for friendship'.

questions.question: Why was Jumman confident of winning initially?

options.B: He thought Algu's talk about being fair was mere show for his friend.

questions.explanation: He imagined that Algu’s talk was mere show.

questions.question: What did Algu do that Jumman found hard to answer?

options.D: He looked at him with disgust.

questions.explanation: Algu Chaudhuri started asking questions which Jumman found hard to answer.

questions.question: What was the final judgement given by Algu in the first panchayat?

options.A: Jumman should get the property back.
options.B: Jumman should pay his aunt a monthly allowance.
options.C: The aunt should leave the village.
options.D: Algu and Jumman should no longer be friends.

questions.explanation: The decision was that 'aunt should have a monthly allowance'.

questions.question: What was the consequence if Jumman refused to pay the monthly expenses?

options.B: The property should be returned to the aunt.
options.C: He would be expelled from the village.
options.D: He would have to pay a fine of a hundred pesos.

questions.explanation: Algu said, 'If you do not agree to pay the monthly expenses, then the property should be returned to her'.

questions.question: How did the judgement affect the friendship between Jumman and Algu?
questions.explanation: The text states, 'It broke up the friendship between Jumman and Algu'.

questions.question: What did Jumman begin to think of after the first panchayat?
questions.explanation: Jumman began to think of taking revenge.

questions.question: Where had Algu bought his beautiful pair of bullocks from?
questions.explanation: Algu had bought a pair of bullocks from the fair at Batesar.

questions.question: What happened to one of Algu's bullocks?

options.B: It happened to die a month after the panchayat.
options.C: It was sold to Samjhoo Sahu immediately.
options.D: It ran away to the hills.

questions.explanation: One of these bullocks happened to die only a month after Jumman’s panchayat.

questions.question: What did Jumman say when he heard about the death of Algu's bullock?

options.B: This is punishment for his deception.
options.C: I will buy the other one.

questions.explanation: Jumman exclaimed among friends, 'This is punishment for his deception'.

questions.question: What did Algu suspect regarding the death of his bullock?
questions.explanation: Algu suspected that Jumman had poisoned his bullock.

questions.question: Who was Samjhoo Sahu?

options.B: An ekka driver in the village

questions.explanation: Samjhoo Sahu was a person in the village who used to drive an ekka.

questions.question: What items did Samjhoo Sahu carry to the town market?

options.D: Raw mutton and cod liver oil

questions.explanation: He would carry ghee and sugar to the town market.

questions.question: What items did Samjhoo Sahu bring back from the town to sell in the village?
questions.explanation: He would return from there with a lot of salt and oil to sell in the village.

questions.question: How much time did Sahu promise to pay the price of the bullock to Algu?
questions.explanation: Sahu promised to pay off the price in a month’s time.

questions.question: How many trips a day did Sahu begin making with the new bullock?
questions.explanation: Samjhoo Sahu began making three to four trips per day.

questions.question: What did Sahu neglect while overworking the bullock?
questions.explanation: He worried neither about giving it fodder nor water.

questions.question: What phrase describes the bullock's physical state after a month with Sahu?

options.B: A mere bag of skin and bones

questions.explanation: Within a month the bullock became a 'mere bag of skin and bones'.

questions.question: What happened during the fourth trip one evening?

options.B: The bullock fell down and never rose again.

questions.explanation: The bullock made a last effort, but fell down on the ground, never to rise again.

questions.question: What did Sahu use to hit the tired bullock?
questions.explanation: Sahuji whipped it with the greatest cruelty.

questions.question: Why did Sahu and his wife refuse to pay Algu for the bullock?

options.B: They claimed Algu gave them a 'dying bullock'.
options.C: Algu hadn't asked for the money.
options.D: Jumman told them not to pay.

questions.explanation: Both said angrily, 'He gave us a dying bullock and now wants the price for it'.

questions.question: What was the price Algu asked for his bullock?
questions.explanation: Algu worried about losing 'a hundred and fifty rupees'.

questions.question: Who helped Samjhoo Sahu against Algu?
questions.explanation: Algu had many enemies. They too gathered and helped Sahuji.

questions.question: When did the second panchayat meet?
questions.explanation: Three days after this, the panchayat again met under the same tree.

questions.question: Who did Samjhoo Sahu choose as the panch for his case?
questions.explanation: Samjhoo thundered: 'Jumman Sheikh on my behalf'.

questions.question: What realization came over Jumman when he became the judge?

options.A: He could finally take his revenge.
options.B: Whatever he says will be the voice of God and he must stick to truth.
options.D: He should return the property to his aunt.

questions.explanation: Jumman thought, 'Whatever I say now will be the voice of God. I should stick to the truth'.

questions.question: What was Jumman's decision in the second panchayat?

options.B: Samjhoo ought to pay the full price of the bullock.
options.C: Algu should pay Sahu a fine.

questions.explanation: Jumman gave the decision: 'Samjhoo ought to pay the full price of the bullock'.

questions.question: According to Jumman, why did the bullock die?

options.B: Because it was driven too hard and not fed properly.

questions.explanation: Jumman stated, 'The bullock died only because it was driven too hard and no proper arrangement was made to feed it'.

questions.question: What did Algu shout after hearing the second judgement?

options.B: Long live the God that is the panch!

questions.explanation: Algu gave a loud cheer: 'Long live the God that is the panch!'.

questions.question: What did Jumman do after the panchayat session ended?

options.B: He approached Algu and embraced him.
options.D: He went to see his aunt.

questions.explanation: Jumman approached Algu and embraced him.

questions.question: Jumman said that after Algu's first decision, he had become his ________.
questions.explanation: Jumman admitted, 'After you gave your decision, I had become your mortal enemy'.

questions.question: What 'washed away the dust' in Algu and Jumman's eyes?
questions.explanation: The text says, 'The tears washed away all the dust in their eyes'.

questions.question: What does the word 'Panch' refer to in the story?
questions.explanation: The 'panch' are the members of the village council or the judges.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'trust' in the glossary?
questions.explanation: Glossary: Trust - to have faith in.

questions.question: What does 'persuade' mean?
questions.explanation: Glossary: Persuade - to convince.

questions.question: The word 'deception' means:
questions.explanation: Glossary: deception - misleading.

questions.question: What is 'fodder'?
questions.explanation: Glossary: fodder - food for animals.

questions.question: The term 'mortal' refers to something that ________.

options.B: Must die or cannot live forever

questions.explanation: Glossary: mortal - which must die or cannot live for ever.

questions.question: The aunt had been treated with 'great ________' until the property was transferred.
questions.explanation: The aunt had been treated with great kindness and respect.

questions.question: What did the aunt mean by 'Separately' when talking about cooking?

options.B: Cooking her own food apart from Jumman's family

questions.explanation: She requested money to cook and eat separately from Jumman's family.

questions.question: Why did Jumman want a decision from the panchayat himself?

options.D: He wanted to move to town.

questions.explanation: Jumman said, 'I also would like a decision. I hate these daily quarrels myself'.

questions.question: How did Algu feel after the old woman left his house initially?

options.B: Troubled, as her words echoed in his heart

questions.explanation: Her words continued to echo in his heart.

questions.question: In the first panchayat, whom did Jumman address angrily, saying 'It is your show'?
questions.explanation: Jumman answered his aunt angrily, 'It is your show. Have anyone you like'.

questions.question: What is an 'ekka' as mentioned in Part III?
questions.explanation: Samjhoo Sahu used to drive an 'ekka' to the town.

questions.question: Why did Samjhoo Sahu buy the bullock from Algu?

options.B: He thought he could make three trips a day easily with it

questions.explanation: He thought if he had this bullock, he could make three trips a day easily.

questions.question: Samjhoo Sahu put a '________ load' on the bullock during the fateful fourth trip.
questions.explanation: One evening Sahuji put a double load on it during the fourth trip.

questions.question: In the second panchayat, Algu told Sahu to have 'his own ________' for the panch.
questions.explanation: Algu replied : 'Let Sahu have his own choice'.

questions.question: What 'voice' did Jumman feel he represented as a judge?
questions.explanation: Jumman thought, 'Whatever I say now will be the voice of God'.

questions.question: What is the central theme of 'The Village Judge'?

options.B: The impartiality of justice and that the voice of the panch is the voice of God

questions.explanation: The story emphasizes that the 'God lives in the heart of the panch' and justice must be impartial regardless of friendship or enmity.

questions.question: Who thundered 'Jumman Sheikh on my behalf'?
questions.explanation: Samjhoo stood up and thundered : 'Jumman Sheikh on my behalf'.

questions.question: What was the 'total loss' that Algu faced according to Sahu?

options.D: The money owed to the aunt

questions.explanation: Sahu claimed Algu gave him a dying bullock, and thus refused to pay for the loss.

questions.question: The tears of Algu and Jumman '________ away all the dust in their eyes'.
questions.explanation: The text uses the phrase 'The tears washed away all the dust in their eyes'.
